newsitem.title: FRANCE: TENNIS-SPANISH ARMADA BLOWN OFF COURSE.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SPANISH ARMADA BLOWN OFF COURSE.

text.p: South Africa's Amanda Coetzer and Belgium qualifier Filip Dewulf laid to rest two of the last remaining Spanish hopes on the red clay of Roland Garros with upset fourth round wins at the French Open on Sunday.

Coetzer, the 11th seed, won a three-set battle over Spain's Conchita Martinez to set up a possible quarter-final clash with Steffi Graf, while Dewulf swept past Alex Corretja, one of the pre-tournament favourites, on a windswept centre court.
Coetzer's 6-7 6-4 6-3 win required huge determination and will not come as welcome news for Graf.

The tiny South African has had the German's number this season, beating her in two of three meetings, including an embarrassing 6-0 6-1 drubbing at the German Open and a straight sets fourth round win at the Australian Open.
In a match that changed directions as many times as the gusty wind, Coetzer needed two hours and 43 minutes to record her first win in 11 meetings with the Spaniard.
"It was tough, extremely windy, at times it was even tough to see," said Coetzer. "I rank this up there among my best wins.
"Before today I had never beaten her, I don't think I had even taken a set from her."
After breezing through her opening three matches without dropping a set, Coetzer looked ready to cruise into the final eight at Roland Garros for the second straight year as she jumped to a 5-2 lead.

But Martinez, the 1994 Wimbledon champion, stormed back to take a 6-5 lead, forcing Coetzer to fight off six set points before going to a tie-break. The Spaniard eventually took the set in one hour and 22 minutes.
"I started off well but I think she knew that she had always beaten me and was full of confidence," said Coetzer. "After I lost the first set I thought 'Here we go again.'
"But she let me back into the match, there wasn't really a whole lot that I did."
Trailing 4-1 in the second, the 25-year-old South African broke Martinez three times winning the next five games and the set.
The battle continued to fluctuate in the decisive set, the two women trading breaks twice before Coetzer finally wrested control to end Martinez's bid for a ninth consecutive semifinal appearance.

While Coetzer's appearance in the next round is not a major surprise, the same cannot be said about Dewulf who became the first Belgian to reach a Grand Slam quarter-final in the Open era with his stunning 5-7 6-1 6-4 7-5 over the eighth seeded Corretja.
Dewulf, ranked 122 in the world, took advantage of the Spaniard's uncertainty in the windy conditions to clinch the most significant win of his career in two hours 57 minute.

"I came here to play the qualifying and I'm in the quarter-finals, it's totally unexpected," said Dewulf, who had failed to advance beyond the second round in previous Grand Slam events. "I gave my all because I had nothing to lose.
"When I won the second set I started to realise I could win the match."
